node_types.label: Country
node_types.description: A country from the reference data, identified by its ISO 3166-1 code.

node_types.label: Currency
node_types.description: A currency, identified by its ISO 4217 code wherever a record names one.

node_types.label: Sector
node_types.description: A section of the ISIC Rev. 4 classification (the level above its divisions).

node_types.label: Industry
node_types.description: An ISIC Rev. 4 division from the reference data.

node_types.label: Company
node_types.description: A company. Every company in the sample network is fictional.

node_types.label: Economic variable
node_types.description: The definition of a measurable economic quantity, such as a price or a rate.

node_types.label: Data series
node_types.description: A provider's time series (e.g. a World Bank indicator for one country).

node_types.label: Instrument
node_types.description: A listed security from a price file a user imported.

node_types.label: Market
node_types.description: A trading venue, identified by its ISO 10383 market identifier code (MIC).

edge_types.label: supplies
edge_types.description: The source provides goods or services that the target uses as inputs.
edge_types.caveat: A recorded supply relationship. It does not say how large or how important it is.

edge_types.label: lends to
edge_types.description: The source (a lender) provides credit facilities to the target.
edge_types.caveat: A recorded lending relationship. It says nothing about amounts, terms or risk.

edge_types.label: competes with
edge_types.description: Both entities sell similar products or services in the same market.
edge_types.caveat: The two sell similar products in the same market; it does not rank them.

edge_types.label: affects costs of
edge_types.description: Changes in the source variable are assumed to change the target's operating or input costs.
edge_types.caveat: An assumed effect, not a measured one: it says nothing about size or timing, and entities of the same kind can be affected very differently. A connection is not evidence of causation.

edge_types.label: affects revenue of
edge_types.description: Changes in the source variable are assumed to change the target's revenue, through prices, volumes or currency translation.
edge_types.caveat: An assumed effect, not a measured one: it says nothing about size or timing, and entities of the same kind can be affected very differently. A connection is not evidence of causation.

edge_types.label: affects financing costs of
edge_types.description: Changes in the source variable are assumed to change the target's cost of borrowing or refinancing.
edge_types.caveat: An assumed effect, not a measured one: it says nothing about size or timing, and entities of the same kind can be affected very differently. A connection is not evidence of causation.

edge_types.label: influences
edge_types.description: Changes in the source variable are assumed to transmit to the target variable.
edge_types.caveat: Assumed transmission between two variables, not a statistical or causal estimate. A connection is not evidence of causation.

edge_types.label: operates in
edge_types.description: The company's primary industry (derived from the company record).
edge_types.caveat: A primary-industry classification. A company can also operate in other industries.

edge_types.label: is domiciled in
edge_types.description: The company's country of domicile (derived from the company record).
edge_types.caveat: Country of domicile only — not where the company sells, produces or is exposed.

edge_types.label: is measured for
edge_types.description: The economy the variable describes (derived from the variable record).
edge_types.caveat: The economy the variable describes. It does not mean the variable matters only there.

edge_types.label: belongs to
edge_types.description: The industry's ISIC Rev. 4 division belongs to this ISIC section.
edge_types.caveat: A classification hierarchy: every division sits in exactly one section. It says nothing about economic links between industries of the same section.

edge_types.label: has currency
edge_types.description: The country's currency, by its ISO 4217 code.
edge_types.caveat: It says nothing about exchange-rate exposure, or about other places that use the currency.

edge_types.label: covers
edge_types.description: The series describes this country's economy, as the provider defines it.
edge_types.caveat: The provider's geography, not a statement about influence between the series and the country.

edge_types.label: is a related measure of
edge_types.description: A curator recorded the series as a related measure of the variable, stating how the two differ.
edge_types.caveat: A related measure, not the same measure: frequency, definition or source differ (see the stated difference).

edge_types.label: is expressed in
edge_types.description: The currency the series' unit is stated in.
edge_types.caveat: Values are shown as published and never converted.

edge_types.label: is listed on
edge_types.description: The market the instrument's prices come from, as declared in its price-file manifest.
edge_types.caveat: Declared by the importer; RUMIN did not verify the listing.

edge_types.label: is quoted in
edge_types.description: The currency of the instrument's prices, as declared in its price-file manifest.
edge_types.caveat: Declared by the importer; prices are never converted.

edge_types.label: is associated with
edge_types.description: The price-file manifest links the instrument to this country.
edge_types.caveat: The manifest does not say how (country of listing, of the issuer, or other).

evidence_statuses.label: Evidence-backed
evidence_statuses.definition: Stated by a cited external source or standard (a classification, an ISO code, a provider's metadata). RUMIN transcribed it; it did not measure or validate it.

evidence_statuses.label: Analyst-created
evidence_statuses.definition: Written by a RUMIN curator, with its reasoning recorded — for example a fictional company's industry, or a series recorded as a related measure of a variable.

evidence_statuses.label: Model assumption
evidence_statuses.definition: An assumed economic relationship with a written rationale. It is not an empirical finding and has not been validated.

evidence_statuses.label: Unverified
evidence_statuses.definition: Declared in data supplied to RUMIN (for example a price-file manifest). Recorded as declared; RUMIN could not check it.

construction_rules.name: country
construction_rules.description: One node per country record.

construction_rules.name: currency
construction_rules.description: One node per ISO 4217 code named by any record; records naming the same code are linked to the same node.

construction_rules.name: sector
construction_rules.description: One node per ISIC Rev. 4 section that contains an industry's division.

construction_rules.name: industry
construction_rules.description: One node per industry record.

construction_rules.name: company
construction_rules.description: One node per company record.

construction_rules.name: economic_variable
construction_rules.description: One node per variable definition.

construction_rules.name: data_series
construction_rules.description: One node per catalogued series, whether or not values have been retrieved.

construction_rules.name: instrument
construction_rules.description: One node per imported instrument.

construction_rules.name: market
construction_rules.description: One node per ISO 10383 MIC declared in a price-file manifest.

construction_rules.name: curated_relationship
construction_rules.produces: an edge of the relationship's own type
construction_rules.description: Each curated relationship becomes an edge of the same type, keeping its description, rationale, assumed polarity and illustrative strength.

construction_rules.name: company_industry
construction_rules.description: A company's primary industry, as written in its record.

construction_rules.name: company_country
construction_rules.description: A company's country of domicile, as written in its record.

construction_rules.name: variable_country
construction_rules.description: The economy a variable describes, as written in its definition.

construction_rules.name: industry_sector
construction_rules.description: An ISIC Rev. 4 division belongs to the section whose division range contains it.

construction_rules.name: country_currency
construction_rules.description: A country's ISO 4217 currency, as cited in its record.

construction_rules.name: series_country
construction_rules.description: The country a series describes: its catalogue link, or else its ISO alpha-3 code when that code already identifies exactly one country node.

construction_rules.name: series_variable
construction_rules.description: A curator's link from a series to a variable, kept with the stated difference.

construction_rules.name: series_currency
construction_rules.description: The currency of a series' unit.

construction_rules.name: instrument_market
construction_rules.description: The market declared for an instrument in its price-file manifest.

construction_rules.name: instrument_currency
construction_rules.description: The currency declared for an instrument's prices in its manifest.

construction_rules.name: instrument_country
construction_rules.description: The country a manifest links an instrument to (the manifest does not say how).

validation_rules.subject: node
validation_rules.description: The source record has no ID, so no stable node key can be made.

validation_rules.subject: node
validation_rules.description: The record has no name to display.

validation_rules.subject: node
validation_rules.description: The node would have no source record to explain it.

validation_rules.subject: node
validation_rules.description: A code that would identify a currency, sector or market is not valid in its scheme, so no node is made for it (and no edge leads to it).

validation_rules.subject: node
validation_rules.description: The industry's code is not a division of ISIC Rev. 4, so it is given no sector.

validation_rules.subject: node
validation_rules.description: The node has no edge to any other node.

validation_rules.subject: identifier
validation_rules.description: An identifier is not in its scheme's format; it is not attached to the node.

validation_rules.subject: identifier
validation_rules.description: The same identifier is claimed for different nodes; it is attached to none of them and the nodes are flagged for review.

validation_rules.subject: resolution
validation_rules.description: Two records of a kind RUMIN never merges automatically share an identifier. Both are kept and flagged for review.

validation_rules.subject: resolution
validation_rules.description: Two records' names are identical once normalised. Both are kept and flagged for review: a name alone never merges entities.

validation_rules.subject: resolution
validation_rules.description: Every word of one name appears in another (often a parent and a subsidiary, which are different entities). Noted for review; nothing is merged.

validation_rules.subject: resolution
validation_rules.description: An instrument's name is similar to a company's. They are not linked: a similar name is not evidence that the company issued the instrument.

validation_rules.subject: resolution
validation_rules.description: Similar names, but one record is fictional or sample data and the other is not, so they cannot be the same entity.

validation_rules.subject: edge
validation_rules.description: The relationship type has no definition in the graph's type registry.

validation_rules.subject: edge
validation_rules.description: The edge's source does not exist in the graph.

validation_rules.subject: edge
validation_rules.description: The edge's target does not exist in the graph.

validation_rules.subject: edge
validation_rules.description: The edge points the wrong way: its type is defined from the target's kind to the source's kind.

validation_rules.subject: edge
validation_rules.description: The edge's type is not defined between these kinds of node.

validation_rules.subject: edge
validation_rules.description: The edge connects a node to itself.

validation_rules.subject: edge
validation_rules.description: The edge has no evidence record, so nothing could explain why it exists.

validation_rules.subject: edge
validation_rules.description: The edge's evidence status is not allowed for its type (e.g. an assumed variable-to-variable effect claimed as evidence-backed).

validation_rules.subject: edge
validation_rules.description: The validity period ends before it starts.

validation_rules.subject: edge
validation_rules.description: The validity period starts in the future.

validation_rules.subject: edge
validation_rules.description: The edge would mix fiction and fact: an evidence-backed edge touching a fictional or sample node, or a business relationship between a fictional and a real company.

validation_rules.subject: edge
validation_rules.description: More than one record states the same relationship; it is stored once, with every record as evidence.

validation_rules.subject: edge
validation_rules.description: A record refers to an entity that is not in the graph, so no edge was made.
